prompt:
Research YouTube's officially documented upload limits: maximum file size and maximum video length, and how to upload longer videos. Cite YouTube's own help page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on YouTube's official help documentation, the platform imposes specific technical limits on uploads, with longer durations requiring account verification.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en | QUOTE: "The maximum file size you can upload is 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less." | CLAIM: YouTube's absolute upload ceiling is 256 gigabytes or 12 hours of duration, whichever threshold is reached first.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en | QUOTE: "By default, you can upload videos that are up to 15 minutes long. Verified accounts can upload videos longer than 15 minutes." | CLAIM: Unverified accounts face a 15-minute duration cap, but verifying the account removes this restriction to enable longer uploads.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en | QUOTE: "1. On a computer, go to https://www.youtube.com/verify.
2. Follow the steps to verify your Google Account. You can choose to get a verification code through a text message on a mobile device or an automated voice call." | CLAIM: To upload videos exceeding 15 minutes, users must verify their Google Account via the youtube.com/verify portal using either SMS text message or an automated voice call to receive a verification code.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/71673?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en | QUOTE: "If your video is larger than 256 GB, try compressing your video in a video editing software before uploading it to YouTube. Use the H.264 codec to compress your video file size while maintaining the video quality for YouTube." | CLAIM: If a file exceeds the 256 GB limit, YouTube officially recommends compressing it using the H.264 codec in video editing software before attempting to upload.
